## 38. Payment, subscription, and nutritionist-compensation architecture (2026-09-05)

**Requirement ID:** REQ-021

**Decision ID:** ADR-017

**Change ID:** CHG-20260905-04

**Verification ID:** TEST-078

### Accepted architecture

- PayMongo is selected as the first sandbox collection adapter. Production remains blocked on written provider acceptance of NutriMind's exact business model, actual subscription/payment capability activation, final commercial terms, Philippine accounting/legal decisions, security review, operations evidence, and explicit owner go-live approval.
- Collection, durable entitlement grants, and nutritionist compensation are separate auditable domains. A browser redirect or client flag never grants Premium, and a user subscription payment never directly triggers reviewer pay.
- The sandbox MVP defines one monthly Premium test price, with PHP 199.00 allowed only as a demo placeholder. Free retains every safety, restriction, verification, weekly planning, logging, grocery/PDF, compatible-library, and account-export capability. The only MVP Premium behavior is a safety-bounded weekly swap cap of six instead of the existing three.
- Paid invoice periods create durable grants through verified webhooks or server reconciliation. Cancellation stops renewal while preserving the paid period; past-due grace is bounded to 72 hours; incomplete and unpaid states create no new grant; refund effects are explicit rather than silently inferred.
- A future raw-body PayMongo webhook route must precede the current global `express.json()` middleware. It verifies the environment-specific HMAC over the exact bytes, persists an immutable event and outbox item before 2xx, processes idempotently, does not assume delivery order, and reconciles missed or exhausted events independently.
- The proposed additive data design covers immutable products/prices, provider customers, subscriptions, invoices, payment attempts, financial ledger entries, refunds, entitlement grants, webhook envelopes/processing attempts, and reconciliation issues. No schema or migration was created in this phase.
- Nutritionist work credits are first-class records written transactionally with eligible completed review actions. Claims, mutable `totalVerified`, duplicates, outcome type, and raw approval volume are not payroll evidence. Compensation uses a contracted base retainer plus capped workload-band allowance plus independently approved adjustments, with period statements and maker-checker payout records. Capstone payouts remain manual/off-platform and contain no bank details.
- PayMongo merchant `Payouts` and wallet-funded `Disbursements` are distinct. Only Disbursements could be relevant to later worker/contractor payment, and it remains deferred behind a separate ADR, provider approval, legal/tax decisions, recipient-data controls, wallet funding, idempotency, and reconciliation.

### Research, scope, and evidence

- Official provider materials were reviewed on September 5, 2026. The abandoned payment architecture artifact and its claim-level citations were removed from the active branch with the September 22 product reversal and remain available in Git history.
- Provider documentation establishes cards and Maya for automatic subscriptions, separate account activation, immediate first invoice with a 24-hour completion window, once-daily retry for up to three attempts, signed raw-body webhooks, duplicate/retry behavior, test mode, and full/partial refund support. GCash subscription availability, refund test coverage, subscription-specific fees, NutriMind business eligibility, and the legal status of provider invoices/receipts remain explicit uncertainties.
- Repository inspection confirmed no existing billing/subscription/entitlement/compensation implementation; the mutable nutritionist counter and generic audit stream are unsuitable accounting sources; the swap cap is currently hard-coded as three; account export must remain a free privacy right; and the current middleware order requires a deliberate webhook raw-body boundary.
- This change adds and reconciles documentation only. It does not modify source, tests, package files, Prisma schema/migrations, provider accounts/configuration/credentials, the configured shared database, deployed environments, or any payment. It does not start or interact with ports 3000, 5000, or 3030.

### Phased gate and next work

- Phase 0 resolves provider/account, commercial, legal/tax, refund, retention, and compensation-policy prerequisites.
- The next single bounded coding phase is Phase 1 only: additive Prisma schema and migration files plus pure state, entitlement, money, idempotency, and work-credit policies with deterministic tests. The migration remains unapplied and no PayMongo call occurs.
- Later separately gated phases cover disposable/shared migration rehearsal, sandbox collection, immutable webhook processing and reconciliation, the 3-versus-6 swap entitlement UI, internal compensation statements/manual payout records, and finally production readiness.
- Every phase has a disable/rollback boundary. Financial and compensation evidence is append-only; rollback never deletes ledger, webhook, invoice, refund, statement, or payout history.

### Documentation verification

- TEST-078 verifies the new ADR's official-source citations, internal Markdown targets, current traceability IDs, required topic coverage, documentation-only diff, whitespace, branch isolation, and protected-boundary exclusions. All **20** unique external citation URLs use official `docs.paymongo.com` or `www.paymongo.com` hosts and were opened successfully during the September 5 research pass; relative links across all four edited documents resolve locally; the 19-term required-topic scan and `git diff --check` pass.
- The exact edited set is `README.md`, `docs/NEXT_FEATURES_HANDOFF.md`, this engineering record, and the new architecture document. Pre-commit isolation confirmed `feature/payment-subscription-architecture` at exact base `d3c73911a9e9a5e28de47e3fcde94fe2ef530eb2`, while local `main` and `origin/main` both remained `d17b30482398472a02eefd505950f8b42af6b223`. No application test or runtime claim is attached to this architecture-only phase.

## 39. Billing, entitlement, webhook-idempotency, and work-credit foundation (2026-09-05)

**Requirement ID:** REQ-021

**Decision ID:** ADR-017

**Change ID:** CHG-20260905-05

**Verification IDs:** TEST-079, TEST-080, TEST-081, TEST-082

**Documentation ID:** DOC-031

### Additive persistence foundation

- Added Prisma enums and 22 new models for products and immutable versioned prices; provider customers; user subscriptions and cancellation requests; invoices, payment attempts, successful transactions, refunds, and append-only financial ledger entries; immutable provider webhook envelopes with separate mutable processing state; durable entitlement grants and reconciliation issues; nutritionist work-credit awards/reversals; versioned compensation policies and periods; statements with immutable credit snapshots and signed adjustments; and payout records/events.
- All monetary values use integer minor units plus a three-letter ISO currency field. No card number, CVC, OTP, provider secret, bank account, e-wallet credential, or health field is present. Provider resource IDs and outbound operation keys have environment-scoped uniqueness where applicable. A stable opaque billing-subject key allows user relations to be cleared without deleting financial evidence.
- Finance/user ownership uses `ON DELETE SET NULL` only where an identity may later be pseudonymized; invoices, transactions, ledger evidence, webhook evidence, nutritionist work credits, statement snapshots, and payout events use restrictive relations. Existing `User`, `NutritionistProfile`, review, meal, safety, catalogue, and auth columns are unchanged.
- The generated migration `backend/prisma/migrations/20260905180000_billing_foundation/migration.sql` is additive and intentionally unapplied. Its generated portion exactly matches a local schema-to-schema Prisma diff from the `bc07d9a` baseline; 43 explicit PostgreSQL checks add money/currency, time-range, webhook environment/hash, ledger sign, grant, reversal, compensation, payout-method, terminal-reference, and maker-checker invariants that Prisma cannot express.

### Pure policy foundation

- `billing-entitlement.policy.ts` resolves Free or Premium only from valid durable grants. A paid-invoice grant requires `PAID` invoice evidence; an active provider subscription alone provides nothing; cancellation preserves an already-paid period; the end instant is exclusive; revocation ends access; unpaid and unverified invoice evidence fail to Free; and past-due grace is linked to the last paid period and capped at 72 hours. The returned weekly swap cap is exactly three for Free and six for Premium.
- `billing-state.policy.ts` defines explicit transition matrices for subscriptions, invoices, payment attempts, and refunds. Same-state delivery is idempotent, older provider evidence is stale, and terminal/out-of-order regressions are invalid. Failed payment attempts remain terminal so retry uses a new attempt; a failed refund may be resubmitted through its same durable request.
- `billing-idempotency.policy.ts` validates provider/environment/event ID and lowercase SHA-256 payload identity, classifies insert, exact duplicate, or same-ID/different-payload conflict, and creates deterministic bounded outbound operation keys. It performs no signature verification or provider I/O; those belong to the later webhook/adapter phase.
- `billing-money.policy.ts` requires safe integer minor units within PostgreSQL integer bounds, uppercase ISO currencies, bounded cumulative refunds, explicit ledger signs, and overflow-safe sums.
- `nutritionist-compensation.policy.ts` gives each eligible work kind fixed relative units, independent of approve/reject/escalate outcome. Duplicate source actions receive no second award; correction uses a signed append-only reversal linked to one original award. Compensation uses a base retainer, capped net workload units, fixed allowance bands, and approved adjustments. Payouts cannot exceed an approved statement or cross currencies, and preparation/review/approval/submission actors must differ.
- These policies are not wired into the current swap, review, API, or admin workflows. Existing behavior is unchanged; `NutritionistProfile.totalVerified` remains present but is not treated as compensation evidence by the new foundation.

### Deterministic evidence and boundary

- Prisma format and validation pass with a process-local non-routable placeholder `DATABASE_URL`; no configured database connection is required or attempted. The checked-in migration begins with the exact deterministic schema-to-schema diff, contains **22 `CREATE TABLE` statements, 42 foreign keys, and 43 check constraints**, contains no `DROP`, `DELETE`, `UPDATE`, `INSERT`, or `TRUNCATE`, and does not alter any existing domain table.
- TEST-079 through TEST-082 add **32** database-free cases. The complete backend suite reports **303 registered, 302 pass, 0 fail, and 1 pre-existing clinical-policy TODO**. Backend production build passes and rewrites 42 compiled aliases; generated `dist` output remains ignored/unmodified in Git.
- No frontend/shared type changed, so frontend lint/build was not rerun. No Prisma client generation claim is made; schema syntax and relations are established by Prisma validation, while generated-client recognition remains part of a later safe migration rehearsal if needed.
- No migration was applied. No database process or configured/shared/Neon connection, seed, fixture, fake finance row, PayMongo API/account/key, webhook route, Express middleware, UI, server, email, OAuth, Gemini, deployment, or money operation was used. Ports 3000, 5000, and 3030 were untouched.

### Next gate

- The next smallest phase is the ADR's Phase 2 migration rehearsal against a disposable local PostgreSQL database only. It must use the exact committed SQL/checksum, prove schema objects and constraints with rollback-safe fixtures, confirm zero prior-data loss, and clean up the disposable target.
- Applying the migration to the configured shared development database requires fresh bounded owner authorization after the disposable rehearsal. PayMongo sandbox integration, raw-body webhook routing/verification/worker/reconciliation, entitlement consumption, billing UI, and manual compensation workflow remain separate later phases.

## 42. Disabled PayMongo adapter and webhook-intake boundary (2026-09-05)

**Requirement ID:** REQ-021

**Decision ID:** ADR-017

**Change ID:** CHG-20260905-08

**Verification IDs:** TEST-085, TEST-086, TEST-087, TEST-088, TEST-089

**Documentation ID:** DOC-034

### Provider contract and configuration boundary

- Official PayMongo Hosted Checkout, idempotency, webhook signature, event, retry, error, testing, and payment-method documentation was rechecked on September 5, 2026. The implementation selects the currently recommended server-side `POST /v2/checkout_sessions`, Basic secret-key authentication, `Idempotency-Key`, provider-hosted `checkout_url`, and signed webhook authority. Exact source links and two documentation inconsistencies are recorded in ADR-017 section 3.6.
- `paymongo-config.policy.ts` defaults to disabled, permits enabled Phase 3A only in non-production `TEST` mode, requires test-key/webhook-secret shapes plus HTTPS success/cancel URLs, fixes the API and checkout origins, and fixes a 5-second HTTP timeout, 64 KiB request/response limits, and 5-minute signature tolerance. Configuration errors contain key names only. The environment example contains no value.
- The detailed webhook guide uses `Paymongo-Signature` with `t`, `te`, and `li`; a general best-practices page says `X-Paymongo-Signature`. Phase 3A follows the detailed guide and accepted ADR. The detailed event catalogue includes `subscription.activated` and `subscription.invoice.updated`, while the webhook-resource registration list omits them; actual sandbox endpoint registration/delivery remains unverified.

### Checkout and provider adapter boundary

- Added provider-neutral gateway, HTTP transport, checkout-intent repository, and webhook-inbox repository contracts. `PaymongoGateway` accepts only an injected transport; deterministic tests use fakes. The application runtime deliberately supplies no network transport and no database repository, so even valid-looking local configuration cannot contact PayMongo or mutate billing data in this phase.
- The adapter emits only the fixed HTTPS PayMongo v2 checkout URL, forbids redirects, bounds timeout and response bytes, uses server-side Basic authentication and the provider idempotency header, allows only `card` and `paymaya`, sends an opaque reference plus price data, and rejects unexpected live mode or checkout URL origins. It never includes a user ID, health data, or arbitrary metadata and never returns a provider client key.
- `POST /api/billing/subscriptions` is mounted behind the existing authentication, `USER` role, and ready-user prerequisites. The route requires an idempotency header and strict price code. Its injected repository contract owns eligible-price lookup, user scoping, request hash/collision classification, replay, completion, and claim release. Disabled and infrastructure failures return stable sanitized responses. Every result carries `entitlementGranted: false`.

### Signed webhook intake boundary

- `POST /api/webhooks/paymongo` is public by provider signature and is mounted with route-scoped `express.raw()` before global JSON parsing. It accepts only JSON and 64 KiB, parses exactly `t`/`te`/`li`, selects the configured signature slot, verifies HMAC-SHA256 over the exact `timestamp.rawBody` with `timingSafeEqual`, rejects timestamps outside five minutes, and parses the minimal event envelope only after authentication.
- The TEST-only runtime rejects `livemode: true`. The explicit allow-list covers Hosted Checkout paid plus bounded subscription/invoice events. Unknown valid events are marked ignored/quarantined; a repository-reported out-of-order event is quarantined; exact duplicates are acknowledged; provider-event ID/hash conflicts return non-2xx; unavailable durable ingestion returns 503 for provider retry.
- The injected atomic inbox contract receives only provider/environment/event ID, type, livemode, SHA-256 body hash, timestamps, signature-key version, minimal resource ID/type, and disposition. It receives no raw body or full provider payload. Phase 3A does not process any event into subscription, invoice, payment, refund, ledger, entitlement, or compensation state.

- TEST-085 through TEST-089 add 40 deterministic cases. The full backend suite reports **343 registered, 342 pass, 0 fail, and 1 pre-existing clinical-policy TODO**. Tests use synthetic process-local secrets, fake clocks, fake repositories, and fake HTTP transports; they open no listener and use no port.

The committed billing migration checksum remains `a3e8b56ca5f3ea640ecd6fb619230038e26654422c387628792a05f728779563`.
- No PayMongo/provider HTTP request, provider account action, credential, shared/configured Neon query or mutation, migration, seed, financial row, entitlement grant, email, OAuth, Gemini, deployment, application server, browser, or port 3000/5000/3030 was used.

## 46. MealPlan index datamodel reconciliation (2026-09-06)

**Defect ID:** DEF-031

**Change ID:** CHG-20260906-04

**Verification ID:** TEST-098

**Documentation ID:** DOC-038

### Contradiction resolution

- Primary evidence resolves the earlier conflicting reports. Canonical migration `20260831090000_production_workflow_hardening` creates `MealPlan_revalidation_status_idx` on `(requiresSafetyRevalidation, status)` and `MealPlan_highRisk_review_idx` on `(highRiskReviewRequired, reviewApprovalCount, status)`. Git history shows both were introduced in commit `098f71d1d3fb1b1affe200a66ab0d3d80e2d8b20`; its simultaneous Prisma model update added the three fields but omitted both `@@index` declarations, and no later schema commit added them.
- Before correction, generated Prisma metadata mirrored the omission. A sanitized read-only query against the accepted pooled Neon `neondb`/`public` development schema returned exactly both named btree indexes with the migration-defined ordered columns. The prior price-acceptance diff was interpreted backward: “removed index” meant that transforming the physical database into the datamodel would drop the indexes, so it proved physical presence rather than absence.

### Smallest code-only correction

- Added `@@index([requiresSafetyRevalidation, status], map: "MealPlan_revalidation_status_idx")` and `@@index([highRiskReviewRequired, reviewApprovalCount, status], map: "MealPlan_highRisk_review_idx")` to `MealPlan`. The explicit `map` values preserve exact historical database names and prevent Prisma from proposing duplicate default-named indexes.
- No migration was created or edited, and no shared database write was performed. The correction describes existing accepted physical state in Prisma schema and generated metadata.
- Current query evidence differs by index. `scripts/enqueue-legacy-plan-revalidation.ts` directly filters `requiresSafetyRevalidation = true` and `status = APPROVED`, matching the revalidation index's leading equality fields before its scheduled-date predicate. The nutritionist queue fetch currently filters `status = PENDING_REVIEW`, orders by creation time, then prioritizes `highRiskReviewRequired` plus `reviewApprovalCount` in memory. The high-risk index therefore has no direct full-prefix query claim in current code; it remains declared because it already exists in canonical migration history and shared development. Any later removal requires a separately authorized database migration and workload decision.

### Verification and preserved boundaries

- TEST-098 checks both exact schema mappings against the immutable production-hardening migration and distinguishes the direct revalidation query from in-memory high-risk review priority. Prisma format/validation and client generation reproduce both mapped declarations in generated metadata.
- A task-owned PostgreSQL 16.4 database applied all 19 canonical migrations. It contained exactly both named indexes, 19 completed migration rows, and zero `MealPlan` rows. Comparing that migration-derived database with the corrected datamodel reported `No difference detected`; a second local deploy reported no pending migrations. A separate read-only comparison of shared development to the corrected datamodel also reported `No difference detected`.
- The full backend suite reports **365 registered, 364 pass, 0 fail, and 1 unchanged clinical-policy TODO**. Backend production build passes with 47 aliases rewritten, and the offline production-dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities.
- The exact local database, labeled container, network, volume, initially absent PostgreSQL image, generated local credential, and verified temporary directory were removed. Final Docker inventory contains zero containers, volumes, and images; only built-in networks remain and port `55443` is free.
- No shared migration or other write, domain data read, EXPLAIN/ANALYZE/load against shared development, historical migration edit, PSA/DA/DTI import, price data, PayMongo/provider call or credential, Gemini, email, OAuth, deployment, application server, browser, frontend change, or ports 3000/5000/3030 was used.

### Official source, license, and geography preflight

- The official PSA Retail Price Survey page states that it collects retail prices at pre-selected major trading centers and links the eleven category series. Its footer licenses site data/content under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International unless otherwise stated. The OpenSTAT matrix metadata reports `Copyright: No` and identifies PSA as the source.
- The official OpenSTAT API guide documents anonymous JSON POST access, CSV and other response formats, and a maximum of 10 requests per 10 seconds. The current 2018-based/new-geographic-code collection lists matrices `0042M4ARN01.px` through `0042M4ARN11.px`, monthly through 2026.
- Live metadata for all eleven matrices contains the exact selected-city entry `....City of Cebu` with external code `072217000`, distinct from province `....Cebu` (`072200000`). This phase therefore uses City of Cebu directly and does not substitute Region VII, Cebu province, or national data.
- Six bounded API POSTs returned unchanged CSV subsets for City of Cebu, January-August 2026. Exact request bodies, raw CSV bytes, retrieval timestamp, source URLs, CC BY 4.0 attribution, and SHA-256 checksums are committed under `backend/data/psa-openstat/2026-09-06-cebu-city`. PSA's `..` missing marker is preserved verbatim.

### Basket and manually reviewed mappings

- Frequency was calculated from the 51-definition managed catalogue: 195 ingredient occurrences and 36 distinct names. The bounded basket selects well-milled rice, carrot, potato, green munggo, cucumber, tomato, chicken breast, and tilapia. Their catalogue targets account for 93/195 ingredient rows (47.69%) and occur in 44/51 meals (86.27%).
- Seven source commodities have manually reviewed exact raw FNRI identities: `Rice, well-milled`, `Carrot`, `Potato`, `Cucumber`, `Tomato`, `Chicken breast`, and `Tilapia`. Green munggo remains `AMBIGUOUS`, with dried-green and fresh-green FNRI candidates retained because the PSA label does not declare preparation. No fuzzy or label-only automatic mapping is used.
- Catalogue exact-identity coverage is intentionally lower because rice, carrot, potato, and munggo recipes use separate boiled FNRI foods. Tomato, cucumber, chicken breast, and tilapia provide 49/195 exact same-identity rows (25.13%) across 37/51 meals (72.55%). Current source cells exist only for tomato and cucumber among those four, leaving actual available-cell identity coverage at 43/195 rows (22.05%) across 35/51 meals (68.63%).
- The snapshot contains 40 positive observations across five commodities and 24 explicit missing cells. Available period ends span January 31 through August 31, 2026; the importer records those dates and applies no implicit freshness threshold. Munggo, chicken breast, and tilapia have no available City of Cebu value in any selected month. Missing observations are reported and not written as zero, inferred, regional, or national prices.

### Deterministic ingestion implementation

- `psa-openstat-price-ingestion.ts` strictly validates the versioned manifest, HTTPS/source/license fields, unique matrix/commodity identities, exact checksums, request format, RFC-style CSV structure, exact geography/commodity labels, monthly headers, positive decimal prices, and explicit missing markers. Decimal strings become integer PHP centavos without binary floating-point money arithmetic.
- Coverage reporting separates basket selection, exact catalogue identity, and actually available source cells. Counts are checked against the live source-controlled catalogue so catalogue drift fails the snapshot preflight.
- `psa-openstat-price-ingestion.service.ts` resolves every named FNRI food exactly once, preserves ambiguous candidate IDs, inserts or verifies stable immutable identities, and rejects conflicting source/geography/commodity/publication/mapping/observation evidence. Later snapshot mappings/observations create append-only successor links rather than updates.
- `import-psa-openstat-prices.ts` defaults to a database-free dry run. `--apply` rejects non-loopback database hosts until a separately authorized shared-import gate. It adds no route, public endpoint, UI, scheduled fetch, or runtime price repository.

### Disposable acceptance evidence

- A task-owned PostgreSQL 16.4 container applied all 19 canonical migrations and seeded 1,537 current FNRI rows. The committed snapshot dry-run passed, then first apply created exactly 1 source, 1 City geography, 6 publications, 8 commodities, 8 mappings, and 40 PHP point observations. Exact replay classified every row as existing and created zero rows.
- A temporary, clearly synthetic local correction copy changed one cell and retrieval identity only to exercise successor logic. It created 6 new publications and 40 successor observations; every new observation linked its prior active row. Exact replay of the probe created zero rows. The probe is not committed, is not official source evidence, and is removed with the disposable environment.
- Post-probe audit found 12 publications, 80 observations, 40 current rows, 40 rows with predecessor links, 7 exact mappings, 1 ambiguous mapping, zero non-PHP observations, and zero ranges with unequal endpoints. The second migration deploy reported no pending migration, status was current at 19, and datamodel comparison reported `No difference detected`.
- The full backend suite reports **375 registered, 374 pass, 0 fail, and 1 unchanged clinical-policy TODO**. Backend build passes with 49 aliases rewritten. Script compilation passes, and the offline production-dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities.

### Preserved boundaries and next gate

- Shared Neon was not accessed or written. No migration/schema change, historical migration edit, DA/DTI/commercial/crowdsourced source, AI/Gemini price, provider/PayMongo call, email, OAuth, deployment, application server, browser, frontend change, or ports 3000/5000/3030 was used.
- The official observations price purchased raw commodity kilograms. Managed-meal quantities often describe cooked edible grams, and FNRI edible portions do not alone establish cooking yield or retail waste conversion. RISK-024 therefore blocks connecting these observations to meal/grocery cost calculations until reviewed conversion evidence exists.
- A separate shared-development data-import gate is warranted. It should re-check shared price-table state, immutable source metadata, hashes, exact FNRI resolution, expected row counts, and idempotent/rollback behavior. Public/runtime use remains a later phase even if shared import is accepted.

A request is scoped to one user and immutable price, binds its price/method/return configuration into a SHA-256 request hash, holds a one-minute claim lease, reuses one opaque provider idempotency key and reference across retries, and refuses automatic provider retry after a conservative 23-hour safety window. The repository uses a serializable transaction to atomically create one immutable `ProviderWebhookEvent` and its `WebhookEventProcessing` row. ## 50. Verified TEST Checkout reconciliation and payment projection (2026-09-06)

**Requirement ID:** REQ-026

**Architecture decision:** ADR-020

**Risk ID:** RISK-025

**Uncertainty ID:** UNC-018

**Change ID:** CHG-20260906-08

**Verification IDs:** TEST-102, TEST-103

**Documentation ID:** DOC-042

### Provider meaning and implemented boundary

- Official PayMongo Hosted Checkout retrieval, payment, webhook, and Subscription API material was rechecked for this phase. The [Checkout Session resource](https://docs.paymongo.com/reference/checkout-session-resource) defines Checkout as one-time use, exposes payments only to secret-key retrieval, and keeps session status separate from payment status. The [Hosted Checkout quick start](https://docs.paymongo.com/docs/payment-channels-hosted-checkout-quick-start) makes `checkout_session.payment.paid` the fulfillment authority, while the [Subscriptions guide](https://docs.paymongo.com/docs/payment-acceptance-subscriptions) requires a separate plan, customer, and subscription for recurring collection. The accepted Checkout created none of those recurring objects. The local projection therefore records one PHP monthly `ONE_TIME_ACCESS_PERIOD` with `NON_RENEWING` status and no automatic renewal. It does not call or claim the PayMongo Subscription API.
- The processor accepts an injected checkout-reconciliation gateway. This phase adds no runtime network adapter and makes no provider call. Before retrieval, it requires one known TEST `checkout_session.payment.paid` event and an exact immutable `BillingCheckoutRequest` with owner, subject, completed session, request hash, reference, and monthly Premium price. Unknown sessions and invalid local bindings are quarantined without provider access.
- Retrieved allowlisted evidence must remain TEST/non-live, match the exact session and merchant reference, report a paid payment and succeeded payment intent, carry unique payment and intent IDs, match PHP and the immutable price amount exactly, and contain plausible monotonic timestamps. Live, unpaid, processing, unknown, mismatched, impossible, stale, and replay-conflicting evidence cannot create finance or entitlement state.

### Durable processing and atomic projection

- `WebhookEventProcessing` now uses one-minute claim leases with process-local opaque tokens and stored SHA-256 token hashes. Eligible work includes pending rows, retryable failures whose backoff elapsed, and expired processing claims. Attempt count is bounded at five; transient retrieval/storage failures receive exponential retry times, while exhausted and deterministic failures remain `FAILED` with no next attempt and an open `BillingReconciliationIssue`.
- One serializable transaction creates or replays the complete local projection: a non-renewing access record, locally issued paid-period invoice, succeeded attempt, payment transaction, two equal debit/credit ledger postings, and one `PAID_INVOICE` Premium grant with a half-open calendar-month range. Unique checkout/payment/source keys and overlap checks prevent duplicate or overlapping paid periods. A lost lease, binding change, conflict, or constraint failure commits none of those rows.
- Structured ledger batches debit `CASH_CLEARING` and credit `DEFERRED_REVENUE` by the same positive centavo amount. Existing signed legacy ledger rows keep their prior representation. Revenue-recognition releases are outside this phase.
- One-time access has no cancellation operation because it never renews. It stays Premium through the paid period and resolves to Free at the exclusive end instant. Refund submission and entitlement consequences remain unresolved and separate; no refund row or automatic revocation is created. Current [PayMongo refund guidance](https://developers.paymongo.com/v1/docs/refunding-transactions) states that only live transactions can be refunded, so this TEST projection cannot be used as refund acceptance evidence.

### Local verification and remaining gates

- A task-owned PostgreSQL 16 container applied all 21 migrations; a second deploy was empty and status was current. Local acceptance proved two concurrent workers converge to one projection, an exact second event replays without duplicate finance, an expired claim is recovered, a provider-ID replay conflict rolls back without partial rows, unknown sessions avoid retrieval, transient failure persists a retry and later succeeds, every created posting batch balances, paid periods do not overlap, no cancellation/refund rows appear, and entitlement falls back to Free at period end.
- TEST-102 covers success, month-end period calculation, ownership/request/price binding, live/session/reference/amount/currency/status/timestamp/staleness mismatches, deterministic replay, unknown-session short circuit, and retry classification. TEST-103 checks the one-time schema shapes, claim lease fields, reconciliation persistence, and balanced-posting identities.
- No existing Phase 3B provider resource was retrieved or changed. No PayMongo API, checkout, payment, webhook, tunnel, secret, shared Neon database, Gemini, email, OAuth, frontend, deployment, application server, or port 3000/5000/3030 was used. The PHP 199.00 value remains a local TEST placeholder.
- Customer-facing purchase/status/expiry/refund UI, recurring renewal, cancellation, refund policy and implementation, a concrete authenticated reconciliation transport, scheduler/process hosting, shared-database migration, TEST provider retrieval acceptance, live pricing, and production enablement remain separate gates. Premium is available only where a caller uses the existing server-side entitlement resolver against the projected paid grant; no UI claim was added.

### Provider contract and implementation boundary

Checkout creation guidance currently recommends `POST /v2/checkout_sessions`, while the authenticated retrieval reference specifies `GET /v1/checkout_sessions/{id}`. The [retrieve Checkout Session reference](https://docs.paymongo.com/re/reference/get_checkout_sessions) and [Checkout Session resource](https://docs.paymongo.com/reference/checkout-session-resource) state that secret-key retrieval includes payment details; Checkout Session status itself remains `active` or `expired` and is not paid-state authority. The adapter therefore requires one `paid` Payment and its matching `succeeded` [Payment Intent](https://docs.paymongo.com/reference/the-payment-intent-object), in addition to the already authenticated `checkout_session.payment.paid` inbox event.
- `PAYMONGO_RECONCILIATION_ENABLED` is an independent false-by-default capability. It can run only in TEST mode, rejects production enablement, and requires the existing TEST secret without exposing it. `PaymongoReconciliationGateway` fixes the origin to `https://api.paymongo.com`, path to `/v1/checkout_sessions/{id}`, method to GET, Basic authentication, no request body, no redirects, a five-second timeout, a 64 KiB response ceiling, and JSON content type.

Only timeout/rate-limit/server/transport failures are retryable. The existing projection processor uses these classes without weakening its binding, lease, quarantine, amount, currency, timestamp, ledger, or entitlement policies.
- Runtime constructs the processor only when the reconciliation switch is enabled. No route, application bootstrap, cron service, scheduler, or public command invokes it. The committed acceptance script is an explicit operator-only harness and enforces at most one provider request per run.

## 52. Server-authoritative Premium access and USER billing surface (2026-09-06)

**Requirement ID:** REQ-028

**Architecture decision:** ADR-022

**Risk ID:** RISK-025

**Change ID:** CHG-20260906-10

**Verification IDs:** TEST-105 through TEST-117

**Documentation ID:** DOC-044

### Current product and provider boundary

- Official PayMongo Hosted Checkout material was rechecked on September 6, 2026. The [quick start](https://docs.paymongo.com/docs/payment-channels-hosted-checkout-quick-start) still creates Checkout Sessions server-side, redirects only to the returned hosted URL, and names `checkout_session.payment.paid` as fulfillment authority. The [Checkout Session resource](https://docs.paymongo.com/reference/checkout-session-resource) remains one-time use; a cancel return does not cancel or authorize local records. [Idempotent requests](https://docs.paymongo.com/reference/idempotent-requests) retain the first executed result for exact retries and reject changed parameters.
- The accepted TEST product is now defined as one-time Premium access for exactly 30 elapsed days, with no automatic renewal. This decision supersedes the earlier calendar-month projection wording in sections 50 and 51 for future processing. PHP 199.00 is displayed only when an active matching TEST price exists in local billing data and remains a sandbox demo value rather than an approved commercial price.
- Checkout, webhook, and reconciliation switches remain independent and false by default. This phase made no PayMongo/provider request, created no external checkout or payment, and used no key, webhook, tunnel, subscription API, refund, real money, or production mode.

### Authoritative access and quota enforcement

- `GET /api/billing/access` is behind authentication, `USER` role enforcement, and the existing ready-user prerequisites. Its repository filters by the authenticated owner ID and reads a repeatable server-side snapshot. The response is an explicit allow-list containing server time, TEST catalogue, exact current access start/expiry, non-renewal, sanitized verification state, cycle boundary, used/cap/remaining swaps, and checkout availability. It exposes no provider payload, IDs, invoice/ledger internals, health profile, other user, or secret data.
- The central resolver recognizes only a current, unrevoked grant with accepted source evidence. Missing, unpaid, revoked, or expired evidence resolves to Free at the half-open boundary. Free permits three meal swaps per plan cycle; active Premium permits six. Current-plan, option, and swap responses all return the server-derived cap.
- Swap enforcement now conditionally increments the owner tracker only while `swapsUsed < cap`, inside the same transaction as the meal replacement and audit rows. Concurrent excess attempts fail with the stable `WEEKLY_SWAP_LIMIT_REACHED` response and roll back. A Premium expiry or revocation during a cycle immediately restores the Free cap without erasing already recorded swaps.

### USER experience and redirect safety

- Desktop sidebar and mobile navigation add **Premium access**. The responsive billing page shows current tier, swaps used and remaining, exact cycle/end times, active non-renewing expiry, the Free/Premium comparison, TEST marker, and demo price. It states one Premium benefit only: six swaps instead of three. Nutrition safety, grocery, export, and privacy behavior remain available on Free.

## 53. Disabled-by-default billing processing worker and aggregate operations status (2026-09-06)

**Requirement ID:** REQ-029

**Architecture decision:** ADR-023

**Risk ID:** RISK-025

**Change ID:** CHG-20260906-11

**Verification IDs:** TEST-118 through TEST-126

**Documentation ID:** DOC-045

### Processing lifecycle and configuration boundary

- `BILLING_PROCESSING_WORKER_ENABLED` is a fourth independent false-by-default switch. Enabling fails closed in production, outside exact TEST mode, or unless both durable webhook ingestion and read-only reconciliation are validly enabled. Disabled configuration ignores stale tuning values and starts no timer or processor work.
- The server composes the payment processor only through the billing runtime and starts the lifecycle worker after the HTTP listener is ready. Billing work remains isolated from the meal cron and has no public trigger. SIGINT and SIGTERM stop scheduling, abort in-flight retrieval, wait for all batch consumers, close the HTTP listener, and disconnect Prisma. The scheduler uses one completion-driven timer, suppresses overlapping local ticks, adds bounded jitter, and backs off after infrastructure-level tick failure.
- Each tick is bounded independently by batch size, concurrency, and a conservative provider-call upper bound. Multiple server instances rely on the accepted serializable database claim transaction, opaque claim-token hash, and one-minute lease to converge safely. Expired processing claims are recoverable; retryable failures keep exponential durable retry times; deterministic or exhausted failures remain dead-letter `FAILED` rows with an open reconciliation issue. Projection stays one atomic transaction and exact replay remains idempotent.
- `AbortSignal` now flows from lifecycle shutdown through the processor and reconciliation gateway into the native HTTPS request. If cancellation happens after a durable claim, the accepted processor records a retryable sanitized failure before releasing the claim. Logs contain fixed outcome categories and aggregate counts only; thrown provider, transport, database, user, health, and payment detail is discarded.

### Aggregate admin monitoring

- `GET /api/admin/billing-operations` inherits authentication and `ADMIN` role enforcement from the admin router. It is read-only and returns TEST environment, pending/processing/failed counts, retryable and dead-letter subsets, oldest pending age, 24-hour success/failure counts, open reconciliation-issue count, and process-local worker enabled/lifecycle/last-run state.
- The endpoint returns no webhook payload, signature, provider resource ID, payment ID, authorization value, secret, user or billing-subject identifier, ledger row, card data, or health data. Durable queue and issue counts come from PostgreSQL; last-run state is explicitly process-local and resets on process restart. No frontend panel was added in this bounded phase.

### Verification and isolation evidence

- The full backend suite reports **432 registered, 431 pass, 0 fail, and 1 unchanged clinical-policy TODO**. TEST-118 through TEST-123 cover disabled and invalid startup, bounded tuning, overlap suppression, two workers, batch/concurrency/call limits, retry/quarantine/replay outcomes, abort and timer cleanup, sanitized logs, jitter, and infrastructure backoff. TEST-124 and TEST-125 cover monitoring aggregation, timestamp bounds, response privacy, and admin-route ordering. TEST-126 proves cancellation propagation through processor, gateway, and bounded transport.
- Prisma format, validate, and client generation pass. The backend production build and script compilation pass. A task-owned PostgreSQL 16.4 container on loopback port 55447 applied all 21 canonical migrations; a second deploy was empty, status was current, migration history contained 21 distinct completed rows, and database-to-datamodel comparison reported `No difference detected`. No schema or migration changed in this phase.
- The updated local acceptance harness used two real lifecycle workers, the real Prisma claim/projection repository, and an injected synthetic gateway. It proved one concurrent projection, exact replay, expired-lease recovery, transient retry recovery, terminal quarantine, overlap rejection, three balanced posting batches, aggregate operations queries, and zero refund rows. Its seven counted gateway reads were in-memory fixture calls; no PayMongo or other provider endpoint was contacted.
- A bounded disabled-worker server smoke on local port 55557 returned healthy and ready, rejected unauthenticated monitoring with 401, returned only the aggregate allow-list to a synthetic ADMIN, and logged completed SIGINT shutdown. The task-owned container, anonymous volume, newly pulled PostgreSQL image, ports 55447 and 55557, and all temporary processes were removed. Shared Neon, ports 3000/5000/3030, Antigravity, Gemini, email, OAuth, browser automation, frontend code, deployment, checkout creation, webhook registration or resend, provider key use, live mode, and money movement were untouched.

### Remaining gates

- This is source and disposable-local acceptance, not deployed always-on operation or shared-development processing acceptance. Checkout, webhook, reconciliation, and worker switches remain false by default. Shared target preflight/application, hosting-topology restart evidence, alert delivery and runbook acceptance, support/refund policy, approved commercial price, provider production acceptance, legal/tax decisions, recurring collection, cancellation, refunds, other payment methods, and every live/production gate remain separate.

## 55. Ingredient conversion-evidence foundation and exact catalogue coverage (2026-09-06)

**Requirement IDs:** REQ-022, REQ-030

**Architecture decision:** ADR-024

**Risk ID:** RISK-024

**Change ID:** CHG-20260906-13

**Verification IDs:** TEST-130 through TEST-136

**Documentation ID:** DOC-047

### Authoritative source decision

- DOST-FNRI's official 47th Seminar Series abstract reports 173 Philippine yield factors derived by weighing selected Metro Manila foods before and after defined cooking methods. The public abstract does not contain the row-level factors, exact item/preparation protocol, dispersion, or applicable reuse terms. It is recorded as `LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED` metadata and supplies no number.
- USDA FNS Food Buying Guide rows define purchased-to-edible relationships for exact product forms and trim, peel, cut, cook, and drain procedures. USDA ARS Release 2 defines cooking yield as cooked hot weight divided by raw weight for exact meat/poultry cuts and methods. These authoritative US rows do not exactly match the current Philippine PSA commodity plus FNRI catalogue preparation pairs and are recorded as metadata only.
- FAO/INFOODS unit-conversion and food-matching guidelines support explicit denominator, density, identity, edible-portion, and preparation controls. They are methodological references rather than NutriMind factor data, and their publication terms still require a use review.
- The committed strict review artifact contains five sources, one shared access timestamp, source/version/geography/method/factor-meaning/food/preparation/uncertainty/license fields, an explicit omission reason for every source, and `pilotEvidence: []`. No blog, retailer, search snippet, AI output, or inferred ratio is present. The acquisition workflow requests DOST-FNRI's full 173-row artifact, protocols, uncertainty, and written reuse terms before any import.

### Additive evidence model and policy

- Migration `20260906234500_ingredient_conversion_evidence` adds `IngredientConversionSource` and `IngredientConversionEvidence` plus six enums. The source records exact provenance, use status, attribution, version/date/geography/methodology, and artifact hash. Evidence records an exact row/version between explicit `PURCHASED_AS_SOLD`, `RAW_EDIBLE`, or `COOKED_EDIBLE` nodes, direction, source and FNRI identities, preparation codes, units, rational lower/upper factors, uncertainty, effective/observation dates, review, and supersession.
- No price or conversion shortcut was added to `FoodItem` or `IngredientPriceCommodity`. Relations are explicit and restrictive. SQL rejects malformed hashes/URLs, source-use claims without license and artifact checksum, non-positive or inverted factors, invalid kind/basis/unit shapes, missing identity bindings, incomplete review evidence, invalid date order, self/branched supersession, and factors sourced from metadata-only or license-review records. Both new tables reject update and delete operations; corrections require append-only revisions. The migration inserts no row.
- The pure evaluator has no Prisma, network, AI, route, or UI dependency. Clinical exclusion runs first. Eligible paths require reviewed, current, non-superseded exact identity/preparation evidence. Canonical mass/volume conversion does not cross unit families. Forward-only rows cannot be reversed. Duplicate conflicts, cycles, repeat use, multiple valid paths, incompatible bases, malformed/plausibility failures, stale/future evidence, and identity/preparation extrapolation return stable unavailable reasons.
- Bounds compose with integer rational arithmetic. The converted-cost helper consumes safe integer quantities and PHP centavos, calculates the purchased range conservatively, and rounds the lower centavo bound down and upper bound up. Household measure-to-mass evidence must be an exact food and preparation row; no generic cup/spoon density is inferred.

### Exact 51-meal coverage result

- The deterministic report revalidates the checksum-pinned PSA snapshot, source review, and all 51 managed meals/195 ingredient rows as of September 6, 2026. The source basket covers 93 rows/44 meals. Exact raw FNRI mapping covers 86 rows/43 meals. A current exact-mapped price and valid gram/kilogram basis cover 80 rows/43 meals.
- Cucumber and tomato share the same named food identity at both boundaries for 43 rows/35 meals, but the retail basis is still `PURCHASED_AS_SOLD` and the catalogue basis is `RAW_EDIBLE`. They require an explicit edible-yield bridge. Thirty-seven current priced rows for boiled rice, carrot, and potato require a purchased-to-cooked chain. The reviewed conversion-evidence and conversion-usable layers both contain 0 rows/0 meals.
- Whole-meal status is therefore 0 complete, 0 partial, and 51 unpriced. The report lists all 195 missing ingredient rows: 102 lack a source-basket commodity, 7 lack an exact FNRI mapping, 6 lack a current price observation, 43 lack reviewed purchased-to-raw evidence, and 37 lack a reviewed purchased-to-cooked chain. Missing evidence remains visible rather than becoming zero cost or guessed coverage.

### Disposable database, regression, and cleanup evidence

- A task-owned PostgreSQL 16.4 container on loopback port 55453 first reconstructed the 21-migration parent. Privacy-safe count/content hashes were captured for all 64 parent domain tables. Applying the one new migration produced exactly 22 completed migrations. Its file and stored checksum matched at `cf6c15f3f6de31b9b4b7120f3fd716e846cccb0d003a5bffa7b13b5fc24af2a1`.
- The conversion inventory contained 2 empty tables, 6 enums with 25 values, 8 indexes including primary keys, 5 restrictive foreign keys, 10 checks, and 3 triggers. A rollback-only graph inserted a valid source and two valid synthetic conversion rows, then proved seven expected failures for source-use rights, factor positivity/plausibility, review evidence, uniqueness, and both append-only tables. Rollback restored both tables to zero rows.
- All 64 parent-table hashes matched the pre-migration snapshot hash `3747c0740b58c2824570e1a0bcc0505865af3a31e1c75d7c006b9c19e9e171c9`. A second deploy was empty, migration status was current, and database-to-Prisma datamodel comparison reported `No difference detected`.
- The full backend suite reports **447 registered, 446 pass, 0 fail, and 1 unchanged clinical-policy TODO**. Backend Prisma format/validate/generate, production build, script compilation, conversion coverage generation, and offline production dependency audit pass. Frontend lint, production build, and offline production dependency audit also pass with no frontend source change. Both audits report zero vulnerabilities.
- The task-owned container, anonymous volume, newly pulled PostgreSQL image, loopback port, and verified temporary directory were removed. Shared Neon, provider/PayMongo, Gemini, email, OAuth, browser automation, deployment, application servers, and ports 3000/5000/3030 were untouched. `main` and `origin/main` remained at `d17b30482398472a02eefd505950f8b42af6b223`.

### Remaining gate

- No numerical conversion factor is accepted. Before a shared or runtime import, obtain a row-level artifact, explicit intended-use rights, unchanged checksum, and an exact source-commodity/FNRI/preparation match with named review. Shared price import, conversion import, repository/API/UI integration, minimum public coverage, user geography, source precedence, scheduled retrieval, and any Premium budget claim remain separate decisions.

## 56. Nutritionist compensation administration and manual payout evidence (2026-09-06)

**Requirement ID:** REQ-031

**Architecture decision:** ADR-025

**Risk ID:** RISK-026

**Change ID:** CHG-20260906-14

**Verification IDs:** TEST-137 through TEST-142

**Documentation ID:** DOC-048

### Work evidence and calculation boundary

- Work began from exact accepted commit `0b649daf57dcc02ceb519ae34e94741034ecac87` on `feature/nutritionist-compensation-admin`. `main` and `origin/main` remained at `d17b30482398472a02eefd505950f8b42af6b223`.
- A successful ordinary approval, ordinary rejection, or first high-risk escalation writes one `ORDINARY_PLAN_REVIEW` credit inside the same serializable transaction as the completed review decision. An independent high-risk second decision writes `HIGH_RISK_SECOND_REVIEW`. Stable source-action keys make exact replays idempotent. Opening or expiring a claim does not call the credit writer; abandoned and invalid decisions do not commit a credit.
- Corrections append one signed negative `REVERSAL` linked to the original award. Work-credit and statement-credit rows reject update/delete operations. `NutritionistProfile.totalVerified`, subscription payment state, and current mutable meal state are not calculation inputs.
- A period locks one independently activated policy version. The deterministic calculation snapshots all unstatemented period credits, applies the base retainer, caps net workload units before selecting the fixed allowance band, and includes only independently approved signed adjustments. Approved statement amounts and identity fields are immutable.

### Administration and role surfaces

- ADMIN endpoints and the responsive `/admin/compensation` workspace support strict policy drafting and independent activation, non-overlapping period opening and independent closure, statement calculation/review/approval, adjustment approve/reject decisions, reconciliation, append-only credit reversals, and manual payout preparation/approval/evidence recording.
- Policy creator/activator, period opener/closer, statement preparer/reviewer/approver, adjustment creator/checker, and payout submitter/checker constraints are recorded in services and PostgreSQL. The payout request accepts only an idempotency key; its PHP amount is the remaining approved statement amount calculated by the server.
- `GET /api/nutritionist/compensation` derives ownership only from `req.nutritionistProfileId`. `/nutritionist/compensation` shows the signed credit timeline, locked policy/version and period statement, adjustments, and payout status/reference for that profile only. It does not accept another profile ID and returns no user billing records.
- Subscription revenue and compensation are explicitly separate in both role surfaces. Capstone payout records use `MANUAL_OFF_PLATFORM`, store a bounded evidence reference only, and contain no bank/e-wallet destination, provider transfer, PayMongo call, or money movement.

### Migration, integration, and browser evidence

- The one additive migration `20260906235900_compensation_admin_workflow` adds workflow actors, adjustment status/rejection evidence, one-active-policy enforcement, lifecycle/maker-checker checks, append-only triggers, and approved-statement snapshot protection. No accepted migration changed. Its SHA-256 is `56ab3fa1c8d631282383d5a27dc62dba9471796d58ad1c64f442b0ae8c332232`.
- A task-owned PostgreSQL 16.4 container on loopback port 55439 applied all 23 migrations. TEST-142 created four unique eligible awards spanning approve/reject/escalate and high-risk second-review outcomes, replayed one award without duplication, appended one reversal, created two statements, independently approved one adjustment, and completed two manual payout records. Exact approved gross, committed payout, and recorded-paid totals were PHP 230,500 minor units with zero mismatch; provider-bound payout rows and provider calls were zero.
- The database rejected direct credit mutation and approved-statement amount mutation. A second migration deploy was empty, migration status was current, and database-to-Prisma datamodel comparison reported `No difference detected`.
- The full backend suite reports **452 registered, 451 pass, 0 fail, and 1 unchanged clinical-policy TODO**. Prisma format/validate/generate and the backend production build pass. The frontend production build generates both new routes; its first run reported two explicit-`any` and one unused-import warning in the new admin page, which were corrected before final checks.
- Authenticated in-app browser acceptance used local ports 3000 and 5000 after confirming they were free. ADMIN and NUTRITIONIST pages rendered their synthetic records at default desktop and 390x844 mobile viewports with no browser console errors and no horizontal overflow. Each role was redirected to `/unauthorized` from the other role's route. The servers were stopped immediately after acceptance.
- The task-owned container and port 55439 were removed. Shared Neon, provider/PayMongo, bank/e-wallet data, Gemini, email, OAuth, deployment, and real payout operations were untouched. Port 3030 and the unrelated project were untouched.

### Remaining gates

- The additive schema is now applied empty to shared development under TEST-149. Compensation policy amounts in disposable acceptance are synthetic and do not establish a contract, salary, employee/contractor status, tax treatment, payout schedule, dispute procedure, retention requirement, or production approval.
- Creating any work credit, policy, period, statement, adjustment, payout evidence, administrator staffing for maker-checker stages, accounting/legal approval, operational dispute and reversal procedures, deployment monitoring, and any future provider disbursement require separate authorization and evidence. Existing PayMongo capabilities remain disabled and unrelated to this manual record flow.

## 57. Integrated three-role adversarial local audit (2026-09-06)

**Change ID:** CHG-20260906-15

**Defect IDs:** DEF-032 through DEF-036

**Verification IDs:** TEST-143 through TEST-148

**Documentation ID:** DOC-049

### Scope and isolation

- Work began from exact commit `9c4e2497053c4c429093d1edc7e4b13d56950157` on `audit/full-system-e2e`. `main` and `origin/main` remained at `d17b30482398472a02eefd505950f8b42af6b223`.
- A task-labelled PostgreSQL 16.4 container exposed only loopback port 55441. Its main database plus dedicated Premium and compensation databases each applied all 23 canonical migrations. A second labelled container on loopback port 55447 hosted only the payment-projection acceptance database required by its existing safety guard.
- All accounts, applications, health entries, meals, reviews, payment records, compensation records, OTPs, invitations, and payout references were synthetic and used `example.invalid` identities. Ports 3000 and 5000 were used only for the bounded local browser/API session. Port 3030 was checked, left untouched, and never bound.
- PayMongo checkout, webhook, provider reconciliation, billing worker, Gemini, Google OAuth, SMTP, deployment, and live-money switches remained disabled. The payment-projection acceptance used an injected in-memory fake gateway; its seven counted invocations were local fixture lookups, not network/provider calls. Premium and compensation acceptance each reported zero provider calls. The local mail-capture seam avoided SMTP and rejects use outside `NODE_ENV=test` or with a relative path.
- One diagnostic Node command accidentally inherited the ignored backend `.env` before the explicit local URL guard was applied. It issued a count and one synthetic-email `findUnique` against the shared database, found no matching row, failed before its proposed update, and performed no shared write. No further shared access occurred. This was an audit-procedure violation and is retained here rather than omitted from the evidence.

### Three-role and adversarial results

- Authentication exercised whitespace/Unicode normalization, malformed email and password input, duplicate registration races, wrong/expired/resend-cooldown OTPs, successful captured OTP verification, invalid access tokens, concurrent refresh rotation/replay, and rate limiting. The double registration committed one account; concurrent refresh returned one success and one denial; invalid and replayed credentials remained sanitized.
- USER onboarding rejected contradictory goals, separator-only safety input, forged structured fields, and a vague unsupported condition. A mixed condition/allergy/intolerance/avoidance save retained six structured entries, required review, replayed idempotently, and blocked normal features until report acknowledgement. The 51-meal certified library generated a 21-slot, seven-day plan with zero Gemini calls.
- USER runtime checks covered current/detail/cross-owner access, planned-meal idempotency, invalid status, outside-meal missing input, water bounds, grocery projection, progress/history, account export, the Free three-swap cap, Premium six-swap cap, and concurrent cap reservation. A forged checkout-return query remained non-authoritative and left the Free account unchanged.
- NUTRITIONIST checks covered verified-license access, claim ownership/expiry/contention, stale/repeated decisions, rejection, ordinary credits, and two-person high-risk approval. Claim contention now converges at HTTP 200/409; a first high-risk reviewer cannot perform the second approval; completed actions create the expected outcome-neutral work credits.
- The full disposable compensation acceptance proved deduplicated completed-action awards, no claim credit, append-only reversal, policy/period/statement maker-checker separation, signed adjustment, idempotent payout preparation, two owner-scoped nutritionist statements, exact PHP minor-unit reconciliation, immutable approved snapshots, manual off-platform evidence, and zero provider-bound payout rows or calls.
- ADMIN checks covered analytics, user/professional/application lists, strict staged application review and call URL validation, invitation activation/replay, operations/audit views, bounded search/pagination, self-suspension denial, target suspension session invalidation, reinstate/login recovery, billing operations, and compensation controls.
- PostgreSQL outage simulation preserved `/health` at 200 while `/ready` changed 200 to 503 and returned to 200 after recovery. A frontend API outage left the loading gate within seconds and returned to sign-in; the recovered API accepted login again.

### Corrections and regression boundary

- DEF-032 replaces the stale fixed `30` acceptance expectation with `COMMON_MEAL_CATALOGUE.length` and moves the fixture to `example.invalid`.
- DEF-033 centralizes expected review-conflict classification and returns HTTP 409 for ownership, claim, state, second-review, and replay contention instead of HTTP 500.
- DEF-034 introduces one finite 30–300 kg policy, bounded and normalized notes, aligned check-in/legacy endpoints, and transactionally coupled profile/history changes. The pre-fix disposable probe accepted 10,000 kg; the post-fix probe returned 400 with both profile and log count unchanged.
- DEF-035 removes the public statement that budget shapes every plan because the accepted conversion report still has zero priced meals.
- DEF-036 normalizes invalid page inputs, caps list limits at 100, and bounds trimmed search at 200 characters inside admin and nutritionist service boundaries.
- TEST-143 through TEST-148 add deterministic regressions for those boundaries and for the test-only mail capture. They require no database or network.

### Browser and verification limits

- Authenticated desktop browser coverage at 1280x720 traversed all current USER, NUTRITIONIST, and ADMIN navigation routes plus landing, registration, nutritionist application, docs, billing return, and unauthorized routes. Every inspected page reported zero horizontal overflow. Theme change and keyboard Tab focus worked, role-crossing routes resolved to `/unauthorized`, malformed registration showed field-level errors, and no new browser console error occurred. The expected network warning during the deliberate API outage was recorded.
- This full audit did not dynamically re-run every page at 390x844. The connected in-app browser exposed no viewport-resize control and no Chrome browser surface was available. TEST-141 retains prior 390x844 evidence for both compensation pages; responsive classes and production compilation cover the remaining pages statically. ## 61. Responsibility-based source modularization (2026-09-07)

**Architecture decision:** ADR-029

**Change ID:** CHG-20260907-03

**Verification IDs:** TEST-157 through TEST-161

**Documentation ID:** DOC-053

### Refactor boundary

- Work remained isolated on `refactor/modular-architecture`, descended from `feature/engineering-hardening`; neither `main` nor `development` was checked out, merged, or modified.
- The refactor preserved existing controller and route contracts. Large mixed-responsibility modules were separated by feature and operational domain rather than by arbitrary equal-size chunks.
- The dashboard now delegates metric calculation, health summary, meal schedule, and outside-meal dialogs to `frontend/src/features/dashboard`. Nutritionist application, administration, compensation, review, and library behavior use named feature modules. Meal and progress workspaces separate remote/state orchestration from presentation, and the two largest modal groups are isolated from their route views.
- `NutritionistService` is now a stable façade over review, profile, and verified-library services. `UserService` is now a stable façade over profile/onboarding, structured safety intake, and safety recheck services. Existing controller imports remain valid.
- Cohesive policy and evidence modules, including the common meal catalogue and restriction/price-ingestion policies, were deliberately retained as single modules: their size is primarily declarative evidence, not unrelated orchestration.
- `scripts/check-source-architecture.mjs` enforces a 900-line ceiling across handwritten `backend/src` and `frontend/src` modules and is the first root `npm run check` gate. This prevents the previous 1,400-1,600-line monolith pattern from returning.

### Safety and scope

- Source-sensitive regression tests were updated to inspect the new owning module rather than the compatibility façade. No assertion was weakened and no production behavior, schema, migration, fixture, provider configuration, or environment secret changed.
- Docker Desktop's Linux engine was confirmed available after the user enabled WSL support. The backend build stage now installs OpenSSL before Prisma generation, removing the earlier build-stage platform-detection ambiguity while retaining the non-root runtime image.
- The first runtime probe correctly failed rather than being counted as a pass: the frontend standalone output was nested at `/app/app/server.js` because tracing starts at the repository parent, while the runtime command started from `/app`. The Dockerfile now copies public/static assets into that standalone application root and runs from `/app/app`.
- Fresh `nutrimind-web:latest` and `nutrimind-api:latest` images then ran as the unprivileged `node` user in uniquely named disposable containers bound only to loopback ports 13000 and 15000. The web root returned HTTP 200 with the NutriMind page, `/health` returned HTTP 200 with the stable API health contract, and Docker reported both containers healthy. The API probe used synthetic development-only JWT strings and a deliberately unused local database URL; it made no database or provider request. Both task-owned containers were removed afterward.
- This phase does not establish clinical verification, production deployment, shared-database integration, or live payment readiness. Those gates remain separate from maintainability and packaging evidence.

### Verification results

- The final source audit found no handwritten TypeScript or JavaScript module above the enforced 900-line ceiling. The largest remaining modules are bounded feature views, domain services, or cohesive declarative catalogues rather than the prior mixed-responsibility monoliths.
- The complete root `npm run check` gate passed after modularization: source architecture, Prettier, backend and frontend lint with zero warnings, **471 registered backend tests / 470 pass / 0 fail / 1 unchanged clinical-policy TODO**, **6 frontend tests / 6 pass**, backend production compilation with 67 alias rewrites, and the Next.js production build with all 42 routes.
- The adversarial public browser wave passed **2/2** Playwright Chromium cases: public entry points rendered without console failures, and registration rejected empty, whitespace-only, and mismatched-password input.
- Root, backend, and frontend dependency audits each reported zero known vulnerabilities at the checked lockfile state. A fresh full `docker compose build` completed for both images after the standalone-path correction, and the final loopback runtime probes returned HTTP 200 from both the frontend root and backend health endpoint.
- Final cleanup left no task-labelled probe container. The working tree was clean at `7f3cb33` on `refactor/modular-architecture`; `main` remained `d17b304` and `development` remained `a77dbd2`. No branch was merged or pushed by this phase.

## 62. Calorie-aligned meal selection and non-blocking dashboard refresh (2026-09-07)

**Architecture decision:** ADR-030

**Defect ID:** DEF-038

**Change ID:** CHG-20260907-04

**Verification IDs:** TEST-162 through TEST-163

**Documentation ID:** DOC-054

### Defect and correction

- Manual testing exposed an approved starter-plan day containing 234, 442, and 447 kcal meals—1,123 kcal in total—against the user's stored 2,780 kcal gain-weight target. The tracker was arithmetically correct; generation had selected certified library recipes by meal type, dietary tags, goal tag, and safety evidence without testing whether the reviewed serving size could satisfy that user's allocated calorie target.
- A pure calorie-allocation policy now assigns 30% of the daily target to breakfast, 40% to lunch, and 30% to dinner, with a documented fifteen-percent per-slot tolerance. Library candidates outside that band are not silently scaled or selected; they fall through to personalized generation. Compatible candidates are ranked by calorie proximity, usage count, and stable identity without mutating the source collection.
- The Gemini prompt now states the exact target and accepted range for every requested slot. Its response schema rejects non-positive nutrients and meals outside the same calorie range, so an under-target response advances through the existing model fallback rather than being persisted as a successful plan.
- The explicit Meals-page regeneration action now sends a strictly validated replacement request after the existing user confirmation. Replacement skips idempotent reuse but does not cancel the prior plan until the new plan is fully prepared and enters the existing atomic persistence transaction. Ordinary first-time generation and rollover retain their idempotent behavior.
- Dashboard focus and visibility refreshes no longer re-enable the initial blocking loader. They keep the rendered dashboard visible while the current plan refreshes in the background, matching the Meals workspace behavior.

### Verification and scope

- TEST-162 reproduces the reported 2,780-kcal allocation and proves the three observed undersized meals are rejected. TEST-163 verifies filtering, deterministic proximity ranking, and input immutability. Strict request-schema tests cover absent, valid, malformed, and unknown regeneration input.
- The complete root `npm run check` gate passed: architecture and formatting, lint with zero warnings, **476 registered backend tests / 475 pass / 0 fail / 1 unchanged clinical-policy TODO**, **10 frontend tests / 10 pass**, backend production compilation with 67 alias rewrites, and the Next.js production build with all 42 routes.
- No existing plan, meal log, profile, shared-database row, Gemini request, provider request, migration, or environment value was changed during implementation or verification. Persisted undersized plans remain historical evidence until the user explicitly confirms regeneration; this change does not fabricate additional consumption or rewrite past intake.

## 63. Account-scoped route data reuse (2026-09-07)

**Architecture decision:** ADR-031

**Defect ID:** DEF-039

**Change ID:** CHG-20260907-05

**Verification IDs:** TEST-164 through TEST-165

**Documentation ID:** DOC-055

### Defect and correction

- Manual navigation testing showed a blocking `Analyzing weekly schedule` or equivalent loader whenever an authenticated user returned to a sidebar destination. Next.js was already prefetching route code, but each route component discarded its API-backed React state when unmounted and initialized its next mount as loading.
- A memory-only session resource cache now retains recently rendered data for ten minutes, namespaced by authenticated user ID. Dashboard, Meals, Grocery, Progress, Health Profile, account Profile, and Billing initialize from that data and immediately render it while their normal API requests revalidate silently in the background.
- Current-plan state is shared between Dashboard and Meals. Meal history and compatible-library results are keyed by their exact filters. Grocery mutations update the cached projection optimistically, and profile, progress, hydration, check-in, outside-meal, and billing state update their corresponding snapshots after successful reads or writes.
- The cache never writes health, billing, or meal data to `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, cookies, or disk. Login, logout, and failed authoritative session refresh clear every entry; owner-prefixed keys prevent one authenticated account from reading another account's snapshot. A browser reload or ten-minute expiry returns to the ordinary first-load behavior.

### Verification and scope

- TEST-164 proves owner isolation, expiry, and targeted invalidation. TEST-165 mounts the Meals workspace, caches one plan, unmounts it as route navigation would, and proves a second mount exposes that plan without a blocking loader while a deliberately delayed server revalidation remains in flight.
- The complete root `npm run check` gate passed: architecture and formatting, backend and frontend lint with zero warnings, **476 registered backend tests / 475 pass / 0 fail / 1 unchanged clinical-policy TODO**, **13 frontend tests / 13 pass**, backend production compilation with 67 alias rewrites, and the Next.js production build with all 42 routes. The public/adversarial Chromium smoke wave also passed **2/2** after the development server was cleanly restarted following the production build.
- This is a client rendering and request-state change only. No shared-database query or mutation, migration, Gemini request, payment/provider request, environment value, deployment, or production action was performed.

**Architecture decision:** ADR-032

They include intentionally separate public profile/privacy projections, endpoint-specific authentication validation and response contracts, semantically different nutritionist-library mutations, static PDF/table markup, client/server date policy counterparts, and meal-card/detail presentations with different interaction ownership. Collapsing those merely to reduce a scanner count would weaken clarity or couple unrelated change paths.

The public/adversarial Chromium wave passed **2/2** after the NutriMind development server was restarted following the production build.

## 65. Item-level outside-meal intelligence and nutritionist correction (2026-09-09)

**Architecture decision:** ADR-033

**Change ID:** CHG-20260909-01

**Verification IDs:** TEST-174 through TEST-183

**Documentation ID:** DOC-057

### Decision and implementation

- Outside-food input now supports up to ten comma-delimited items while preserving spaces and the word `and`; an optional `(150g)` or `- 150g` suffix supplies the measured portion required to scale FNRI per-100 g composition.
- Resolution is item-scoped and ordered: exact compatible/current certified Meal Library evidence, FNRI with measured portion, user-reported label/menu values, explicitly requested Premium Gemini estimation, then unresolved. Unresolved item nutrition is nullable and excluded from totals rather than being represented as a verified zero-calorie food.
- Free retains library, FNRI, manual values, safety context, and notifications. Gemini estimation requires server-authoritative Premium entitlement and is bounded to five items per Manila day and thirty per rolling thirty days. Successful estimate calls are recorded as consumed provider capacity.
- Gemini items count immediately in the daily tracker but are separately marked provisional. Every AI item creates a prioritized review row. An eligible nutritionist must acquire a thirty-minute claim before verifying, correcting, or requesting more information.
- Initial and reviewed values are immutable revisions. Review completion updates the effective item and parent aggregate in one serializable transaction, then notifies the user. Nutrition status and compatibility status remain separate.
- User and nutritionist interfaces expose sources, unresolved exclusions, uncertainty ranges, provisional totals, review controls, and honest Free/Premium differences. The full decision contract is in `docs/OUTSIDE_MEAL_INTELLIGENCE.md`.

### Verification and scope

- Prisma formatting/generation and validation passed with a synthetic local connection string; backend and frontend production builds passed, including all 43 frontend routes. Backend and frontend lint passed with zero warnings.
- The deterministic suites passed: **487 registered backend tests / 486 pass / 0 fail / 1 unchanged clinical-policy TODO**, and **19 frontend tests / 19 pass**. New tests cover comma parsing, measured FNRI scaling, provisional/unresolved totals, Premium and server-configurable quota policy, additive persistence evidence, role/claim route boundaries, and strict mixed-source input validation.
- Disposable migration rehearsal used a task-labelled PostgreSQL 16.4 container exposed only on `127.0.0.1:55461`. ## 66. Administrator-governed nutrition reference data (2026-09-09)

**Architecture decision:** ADR-034

### Decision and implementation

Releases move through `DRAFT`, `STAGED`, `ACTIVE`, and `RETIRED`; only one release per source can be active. Exact FNRI names and verified aliases map automatically; ambiguity remains review-required and unknown labels remain explicitly unmapped.
